Help

GroupToDo stores your tasks, projects, and reference material as plain Markdown files in your own folders. Every change writes directly back to disk. Built on Getting Things Done (GTD) principles, it is designed to get things out of your head and into a trusted system with minimal friction.

Capture & Navigation

  • Capture (N): Press N from anywhere to capture an item to Today's page. Names, contexts, and dates parse automatically as you type.
  • Search (/): Find any action or page, or paste a file path to open it directly.
  • Sidebar (\): Access your core views. Hide with ⇤ or \; reopen with ☰.
  • History (Alt+← / Alt+→): Navigate back and forward across all views and pages.
  • Profile: Click GroupToDo (top left) to view your personal notes, backlinks, and set area-specific profile pictures.
  • Storage & Sync: Click the folder path at the bottom of the sidebar to manage local folders, vault files, and sync settings.

Clarify & Organize (Writing on a Line)

Click any line to write or clarify. Press Ctrl+., or click ⋯ at the end of the line, for a menu to assign GTD metadata:

  • Triggers: Type @ for people, @@ for contexts, # for projects, and [[ for pages. In the box at the top, a context you already have works as the last word too: Call Mia about the VAT phone tomorrow.
  • Auto-linking: Known names are suggested as you type (Tab to accept). Full names link automatically when you leave the line.
  • Aliases: aliases:: JS, Johnny on a person's or organisation's page gives it short names. @js Tab writes [[p/John Smith][JS]], which reads as JS and shows John Smith · Acme on hover; Storebrand written out links to Storebrand Forsikring AS.
  • Dates: Type natural dates (tomorrow, friday, in 3 days) and press Tab. Placing a date at the end of a task sets its due date.
  • Waiting For: Setting a line's state to Waiting prompts you to assign the person you are waiting on.
  • Live lists (/query): A line like {{query (and [[1/Fix sink]] (task TODO DOING))}} shows every line that matches, kept up to date, and its tasks can be ticked from there. The builder writes the query for you; Edit on the list changes it. Logseq's simple queries work: [[page]], #tag, "words", (task ...), (page ...), (property key value), (page-property key value), (between -7d today), and / or / not.
  • Embeds (/embed): {{embed [[page]]}} shows that page in the line, live. For one line, use its line menu → Copy as embed and paste it anywhere: {{embed ((id))}}. ((id)) on its own reads as the words of that line.
  • Sheets: Three tracker kinds take the line as you say it: Hours worked (tracker-office_t:: 07:12 - 10:00, 10:30 - 12:30, with Start and Stop on today's page), An amount (129,50 + 45) and Stock (+3, -1, =12). For hours, one tracker per place you work, like office and home: the year then counts the days you drove in. Trackers > Hours, Amounts or Stock adds them up: a week by day with extra hours and flex, and a year by month, each copied as cells for a spreadsheet.
  • Time per client: A todo set to Doing runs a clock until it leaves Doing (Logseq's :LOGBOOK:), shown as ⏱ under the line. The client is the organisation the project's page or area names. Projects > Hours > Clients adds it up by week and month, with the projects under each client.
  • Last time: On a day page, a tracker or a key:: value of your own shows faintly what you wrote the last time you filled it in.
  • Namespaces: A page in a family, [[Work/Clients/Acme]] or Work - Clients - Acme, lists the rest of the family at the bottom.
  • Duplicate lines: ⋯ beside a page title → Remove duplicate lines. A line written twice under the same parent goes, and what was under it moves to the first copy. The Weekly review says when any page has some, and lists them. Undo puts them back.
  • Dates in the words: In the box at the top, the end of the line is read for when: Call Bob fri 2pm, Pay rent by the 1st, Water plants every monday, in English or Norwegian (i morgen kl 14, fredag), and Taskwarrior's due:, until: and remind: anywhere in it. A toast says what was read, with Keep the words to undo it. A time is written after the day, SCHEDULED:: [[2026-10-23]] 14:00.
  • Reminders: A task with a time gets a reminder 10 minutes before (or remind::, set in its panel), which stays until answered: Open, In 10 min, Done. A birthday gets one on the day. Today shows how long until the next timed task and the next deadline.
  • Letting tasks go: until:: on a task cancels it once that day has passed, and a birthday task (Buy a present for Anna's birthday [[p/Anna Berg]]) goes once that birthday has passed, unless it is switched off in Vault & sync. Being late cancels nothing. Struck out, not deleted, with expired::, and the toast can undo it.
  • A project on hold: the status menu (⇄) has Hold until a day: hold:: on the project's page hides its actions until then, moves it to On hold under the project list and keeps it out of the stuck-projects check.
  • Burndown: the Report shows how many tasks were open on each day of its window, with what was added and finished on a day when you point at it, where the pace leads, and the same numbers as a table.
  • Phone and PC: on a phone, Send (⇧) is in the top bar, with a dot while there are changes the vault file has not carried. Set your working hours in Vault & sync and the PC asks for the phone's file around the start of the day, the phone for the PC's around the end.
  • On hold: hold:: [[date]] hides a task from every list until that day, and then it is back by itself; holding a line holds the steps under it. hold:fri (or wait:fri) in the box at the top, or On hold until in the task panel. The bottom of Next lists what is on hold, each with Bring it back now.
  • Urgency: Next and the project list are in order of urgency by default, Taskwarrior's way: the deadline coming closer, the scheduled day reached, priority:: H/M/L, started, the context you are in, age, being in a project, chat, and the project chain (another project waiting on it counts up, waiting on another counts down). The ↑ chip on a row says why. Priority is in the task panel, or pri:H in the box at the top. The Sort menu has the other orders.
  • Time on site: Type /in on any line when somebody arrives: who, which project and the time now are filled in (the last person and project you used), to change before it is saved as a #timelog line on that day's page. /out when they leave. Gone for a while and back is a second /in. Click the clock under the line to correct it. Projects > Hours (v h) shows each week by day, to copy as text; a project's page shows its hours per week.
  • Meetings: The next #meeting with a time today is shown at the top, counting down, and you are reminded before it starts (Calendars sets how long before, or turns it off).

Engage (Views)

Today

  • Overview: Displays overdue and due-today items first, followed by the next 7 days, then your daily journals per Area. (On wide screens, journals appear side by side.)
  • Focus (Zoom): Click any bullet to focus exclusively on that branch. Use the breadcrumb trail at the top to zoom back out.
  • Fold: Click a section title or arrow to collapse or expand it.
  • History: Next to the date, scroll backward day-by-day through past activity.

Contexts (c/)

  • Contexts represent the tools or locations required to take action.
  • Each context is a page under c/. Click a context to see all available Next Actions for that situation. Add icon:: on the page to give it an icon.

Projects

  • Status by Folder: A project's status matches the folder its file lives in: Active, Waiting for, Someday/Maybe, Completed, or Cancelled. Drag cards on the board to change status; all links update automatically.
  • Auto-Waiting: If all open next actions in a project are waiting on someone, the project automatically marks itself as Waiting for (auto).
  • Timeline (v t): View and drag project bars to adjust schedules.
  • Report (v r): Review completed outcomes by date range. Use Copy as text for status updates.

People & Organizations

  • Delegate: On the People board, pick what a person is dragged to: Projects to involve them, Organisations for where they work, Areas to move, copy or sync them into another area, or Tasks to hand a next action off (moving it to Waiting for). The Organisations board does the same for organisations: Projects and areas, or People.
  • External Updates: Requesting an update from someone outside an Area generates a check-in sheet for them.
  • Where people work: Say it on a person's page (Works at), or name the page Anna Berg - Acme. Two people with the same name can then live side by side, a link to either reads Anna Berg · Acme, and Acme's page lists its people and everything open that names Acme or any of them.

Areas of Focus & Horizons

  • Areas (Horizon 2): Each Area is a dedicated folder (shared with relevant people) representing an ongoing sphere of responsibility. Its responsibilities are pages under a/.
  • Filtering: Use the top-right checkboxes to filter views by one or more Areas. When multiple Areas are active, items display color-coded tags. Click an Area's name to make it the default destination for new captures.
  • Horizons Ladder: Connects daily actions to your overarching purpose. Purpose and Vision live in your primary home Area; Goals aggregate across all Areas. Open any Area in Horizon 2 to edit its specific horizons.

Reflect (Weekly Review)

  • Structured into three GTD phases: Get Clear, Get Current, Get Creative.
  • Check off steps as you go; linked steps take you directly to the relevant tool view. Customize the checklist under Routines & lists > Weekly review.
  • Project Review (Solitaire Mode): Projects are dealt one card at a time, stalest first, and the deck is gone through in three passes, and a fourth for Someday/Maybe:
    1. Status – every project, one question: still active, waiting, someday/maybe, completed or cancelled? Include Waiting for and Someday/Maybe here if you want them looked at too.
    2. Outcome – only what is still active: what does done look like, which responsibility is it part of, when is it due, and does it wait for another project?
    3. Next action – only what is still active: the very next thing to do, who else is in it, and which organisations it is for.
    4. Someday – once the active projects are squared away: two someday/maybe projects side by side, and you pick the one you would rather do. Winners meet winners, as in a cup, so only the best five are sorted, not the whole list: forty projects take about 55 choices the first time. One area at a time, so work and home are never weighed against each other. Activate any of them from the ranking beside the cards. Your choices are kept in the area's GTD.md as someday_duels::, so next week only new projects need placing; a choice older than eight weeks is asked again.
    Why passes, and not everything about one project at once? Each kind of question needs a different kind of thinking. Deciding whether a project still matters is quick sorting; saying what done looks like is strategy; working out the next call to make is tactics. Switching between the three for every project tires you out fast, and a hard next action on project three is where most reviews get abandoned. Sorting everything first is fast and gives early wins: what is done or dropped leaves the deck, so the slower passes only cover projects that still need thought.
  • Every new project is dealt onto the table: the last card's answers are gathered up, the new card slides in face down and turns over, and only then are its answers dealt. You can always tell when you have moved to a different project. Pick an answer by clicking it or dragging the card onto it. A project is stamped reviewed:: once every question is answered, or straight away when it is marked Completed or Cancelled, or stays Waiting or Someday after the first pass. Skip sends a card to the end of the pass; the passes down the side can be dealt in any order.
  • Solitaire keys: the number on a box (numpad or number row) aims at it, and the same number again, or Enter, takes it. The arrows go from box to box, and a letter aims at the answer starting with it. 5 goes back to the project; press it twice to skip it. Shift+→ flings the card on as reviewed. In the Someday pass ← and → pick a side, ↓ skips the pair and Backspace undoes the last choice.

Keyboard Shortcuts

Line Actions

KeyAction
Alt+TToggle between Task and Note
Alt+1Convert line to a Project and link it
Ctrl+EnterCycle state: To Do → Doing → Waiting → Done → Note
Alt+D / C / P / O / J / RSet Due date, Context, Person, Organization, Project, or Repeat
Tab / Shift+TabAccept suggestion / Indent or Outdent
Alt+1 / 2 / 3 / 8 / Z / P / O / C with words selectedTurn just those words into a link to a project, list, zettel, person, organisation or context
Esc, then Shift+↑ / ↓Pick the line, then pick more lines above or below (also Shift+↑ / ↓ at the top or bottom of a line)
Alt+Shift+↑ / ↓Move the line, or the picked lines, and their sub-items up or down
Alt+SMove line to another Area
Alt+IMake it a responsibility: link the line to one, or turn the project into one (merged when it is already there)
Ctrl+.Open or close the line menu
↑ / ↓ / Enter / EscNavigate, select, or close an open line menu

Global Navigation

KeyAction
NCapture a new task
/Search
\Toggle sidebar
?Open Help
TGo to Today
@@Switch current Context
g n · g w · g pGo to Next Actions, Waiting For, or Projects
g c · g rGo to Chat or Weekly Review
g hRecently done: what you finished, to add a comment to
v b · v t · v rView Next Actions as Board, Timeline, or Report
v hHours on site, week by week
v g · v mView Mind Map or Graph
Ctrl+ZUndo last delete or move
EscClose active panel, menu, or Help
